answer.rationale: The two measurable deteriorations are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%); onboarding simplification is the one lever whose inherited evidence (memory_86, reinforced by memory_31) speaks directly to both, since completion and time-to-value feed activation downstream. Promotional pricing is the emotionally obvious answer to the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73's record is the weakest in the set on its face: a four-week window in the 'standard' SMB segment with the 'usual reporting cadence' is long enough to capture acquisition and booked revenue and too short to capture whether discount-acquired accounts retain or expand. Buying price-sensitive accounts at a discount against a competitor who can keep cutting risks importing a low-value, churn-prone cohort and mistaking it for revenue lift, which directly conflicts with the 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective. So I spend verification on the two memories that could actually change my decision: memory_86 (does the completion lift hold up, and did it translate into qualified downstream revenue or just top-of-funnel completion?) and memory_73 (what happened after week four, and was retention ever measured?). I deliberately do not verify memory_91, memory_57, or memory_44, since none of them would flip this week's choice. Two live risks I am carrying rather than resolving: (1) memory_31's mechanism was cutting required signup fields, which can raise raw activation while degrading lead qualification and sales routing, so a 'win' here can be an artifact of measuring the wrong thing; (2) the current declines may be caused by the competitor changing the mix of who signs up, in which case no onboarding change will restore the old numbers and I should not read a null result as onboarding being a dead lever. Standard experiment rather than broad rollout: the supporting memories are 24-52 days old, consolidated into lossy one-line claims, and were established before the competitive shift, so they are hypotheses about the current environment rather than settled facts. I will instrument qualified-revenue and retention endpoints, not just completion rate. If verification shows memory_86 rests on completion-only metrics, or that memory_73 was never followed past four weeks, I will downgrade to a small guarded test and treat the pricing option as unproven rather than as a proven fallback.
